obligation: G115 -- rANS consume-direct kernel inside the geo tile
THIS_IS_A_PREDICTION_NOT_A_MEASUREMENT: No kernel was built and none is claimed. This prices the decode from its ALGORITHM against a measured per-op rate, so that G116 has a falsifiable number to test rather than an opinion.
per_op_rate_basis: NX_MATMUL_K_AMORTIZATION fitted q4 at 5 decode ops against 1 MAC, and G072 measured that kernel at 0.8046 ps/element. That gives 0.1341 ps per op on this machine.

rans_decode_step_counted_from_the_algori.step: renormalise: test state < lower bound, conditional 32-bit load and shift
state update: s = freq*(s>>prec) + (s & mask) - cumfreq
dequant: multiply by the group scale

why_the_symbol_search_is_cheap_here: G114 measured the real q3 alphabet at SEVEN symbols, not eight. A 4096-entry lookup table at 12-bit precision would be the textbook choice and would cost threadgroup memory; with seven symbols a binary search is 3 compares and needs no table in the tile at all. That is a genuine advantage of this particular stream and it is why the optimistic variant is the fair one.
the_predicted_verdict: Even on the optimistic variant, rANS decode is 1.83x q4's ALU per element. That adds 17.180 ms to the token -- 56% -- to save 40% of bytes on a machine G072 measured ALU-issue bound and G094 measured non-responsive to byte traffic. The predicted net is a LOSS, and G116's acceptance already states that a loss is a valid closure.
what_would_falsify_it: If the renormalisation branch is predicated rather than divergent and the binary search folds into a few select instructions, the op count could fall toward 6-7 and the verdict would narrow. That is exactly what building the kernel would settle, and it is why this is recorded as a prediction with a stated op count rather than as a conclusion.
